name: Canadian Shield

geo.extent: Horseshoe around Hudson Bay: from the Arctic islands and Labrador to the Great Lakes and the Northwest Territories

description: The largest physiographic region of Canada: an ancient, glaciated rock surface levelled by long erosion, with an even skyline broken by rounded or flat-topped hills and a great share of its surface covered by lakes, ponds and swamps. The terrain is strikingly similar from Labrador through northern Quebec and Ontario to the Northwest Territories.

subregions: Kazan Region (northern Manitoba and Saskatchewan, parts of NT and NU)
Davis Region (Ellesmere Island to northern Labrador; includes the Torngat Mountains)
James Region (centre of Manitoba to Labrador)
Laurentian Region (uplands and highlands along the St. Lawrence Lowlands from Georgian Bay to the Atlantic)
ecozones_named_in_source: Boreal Shield (plains, some hills; evergreen and mixed forest; cold, moist)
Taiga Shield (plains, some hills; open evergreen-deciduous trees, some lichen-shrub tundra; discontinuous permafrost)
attributes.settlement_note: Settlement is concentrated on its southern margin (e.g. Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Yellowknife); interior access is mainly by air, water and winter road.

sources.title: The Atlas of Canada – Physiographic Regions of Canada (map 1254A compiled by H.S. Bostock, 1967, with descriptive text)
Table 1.4 Biophysical characteristics of terrestrial ecozones (Human Activity and the Environment 2009, archived; from the National Ecological Framework / Wiken et al. 1996)

limitations: Physiographic description summarised from the Atlas of Canada; the map dates from 1967 (Bostock) and boundaries are generalised at 1:5 million. Lat/lon not given because the record describes an extensive region, not a point. Province list and settlement note are agent-04 readings of the Atlas map, not Atlas text.
